summary.text: Raul Ruiz is the Democratic incumbent for California's 25th Congressional District. He is an emergency physician who worked in the Coachella Valley and as a senior associate dean at the UC Riverside School of Medicine before winning election to the U.S. House in 2012. He serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.

paragraphs.text: Born in Zacatecas, Mexico. According to his official biography, he grew up in Coachella, California, where both of his parents were farmworkers.
Graduated from Coachella Valley High School in 1990 and from UCLA in 1994 (magna cum laude, according to his official biography).

Earned a medical degree and a master's degree in public policy from Harvard University in 2001 and a master's degree in public health from Harvard in 2007. His official biography says he was the first Latino to earn three graduate degrees from Harvard.

Completed a residency in emergency medicine at the University of Pittsburgh and a fellowship in international emergency medicine at Brigham and Women's Hospital; during training he consulted for the health ministries of Serbia and El Salvador.

Returned to the Coachella Valley as an emergency physician at Eisenhower Medical Center, started a pre-medical mentorship program that became part of the UC Riverside School of Medicine, and served there as a senior associate dean. He also helped open a free clinic through Volunteers in Medicine and in 2010 started the Coachella Valley Healthcare Initiative.

In 2010 traveled to Haiti after the earthquake and served as medical director for the J/P Haitian Relief Organization; the U.S. Army's 82nd Airborne Division presented him a Commander's Award for Public Service for that work.
Won election to the U.S. House in 2012 in California's 36th District, defeating Republican Mary Bono Mack, and has been re-elected since; the district number changed to the 25th in 2023.

Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (Communications and Technology, Health, and Environment subcommittees in 2025-2026) and previously served on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (2021-2022) and the Natural Resources Committee (2013-2016). His official biography says he lives in Indio.
